text: Operating Systems (OS) form the backbone of modern computing systems. Every application program, from a simple calculator to complex AI software, relies on the operating system to interact with the hardware. Without an operating system, application developers would need to write hardware-specific code, making software development extremely complex and impractical.

If an operating system were not developed, application developers would need to directly interact with hardware components such as the CPU, memory, disk, and I/O devices. This would require detailed knowledge of hardware architecture, device protocols, and low-level instructions.

text: Early computers did not have operating systems. Programs were loaded manually, and only one program could run at a time. Over time, as hardware became more powerful and users demanded multitasking, operating systems evolved to manage resources efficiently and provide better usability.
The primary goals of an operating system are:
Execute user programs and make solving user problems easier
Make the computer system convenient to use
An effective OS balances user convenience with efficient hardware utilization.
Although only a small percentage of computer professionals design or modify operating systems, almost all software runs on top of an OS.
Understanding operating systems is crucial for:
Understanding resource behavior such as memory usage and CPU scheduling
Knowledge of OS fundamentals leads to proper, efficient, effective, and secure programming.
